title: Polyglot SDK Intake & Enterprise Prioritization Framework for Auth and Streaming Ergonomics
creator: Aisha Malik
description:
Summary: Create a repeatable intake and prioritization playbook for polyglot SDK requests from enterprise customers that focuses on language support, authentication patterns, and streaming ergonomics. Goal is to reduce ad-hoc decisions, increase cross-functional predictability, and surface clear trade-offs (engineering cost, security/regulatory constraints, UX, and business impact).

Scope: This ticket covers the triage rubric, intake form fields, stakeholders/decision owners, initial ranked language roadmap, auth patterns recommended for enterprise (token rotation, short-lived creds, SSO, mutual TLS), and streaming ergonomics guidance (handshake, flow-control, resumability, delta updates). Implementation tracking and follow-up engineering tasks will be created as sub-issues.

Deliverables: triage rubric (scoring matrix), intake form template for solutions/AE/CS, recommended 3-wave language rollout with justification, prioritized backlog for auth/streaming features, example acceptance criteria, compliance gating checklist, and a companion Confluence playbook linked below.
triage_rubric: Score 0-5 across: Business Impact (customer ARR, deal risk), Engineering Cost (est. points), Security/Compliance Risk, Usage Signal (customer count & query volume), UX Risk (migration complexity), and Long-term Maintenance.
Thresholds: >=18 -> P0 / dedicated roadmap; 12-17 -> P1 prioritization in next cycle; 8-11 -> P2 backlog; <8 -> P3 or trade-down.
Tie-breaker: enterprise legal/compliance needs trump lower scores if constrained by regulation or procurement timelines.
intake_form_fields: Auth & security requirements (SSO, KMS, rotation, mTLS)
Attachments: contract language, security questionnaire, sample code
language_prioritization_heuristics: Signal-driven: number of customers requesting + total ARR exposure for that language
Ecosystem reach: community adoption and existing unofficial client libraries
Engineering cost: native runtime bindings, test maturity, CI platform support
Maintenance cost: perf regression risk, dependency surface, FFI complexity
Interoperability: alignment with streaming and auth primitives (e.g., async/await vs callback models)
recommended_first_wave_languages: JavaScript/TypeScript - highest product demand and PLG usage
Python - major ML/infra customers and notebooks integration
Java - enterprise backend adoption and JVM ecosystems
Go - high-performance server-side clients and cloud infra
auth_patterns_guidance: Primary: short-lived bearer tokens with rotation endpoint and built-in examples for token refresh flows
SSO/SAML/OIDC: recommended for enterprise SSO; include sample config and session management guide
mTLS: provide optional mutual TLS instructions for air-gapped or regulated deployments
KMS/HSM integrations: document key management approaches for Private deployments
Token revocation & audit: require logs and example hooks for Console to display token usage
streaming_ergonomics_guidance: Handshake & capability discovery: client should negotiate chunking vs event-mode; server advertises maximum window size
Flow-control / backpressure: provide high-level primitives in SDKs (pause/resume, maxConcurrency) rather than exposing low-level tokio/select patterns
Resumable streams: implement idempotent cursors and delta replays for short network interruptions
Delta encoding: recommend payload diffs for high-frequency updates to reduce token costs
Tooling: include replayable examples and integration test harnesses in repo; add an observable metric for stream reopens and partial failures
acceptance_criteria: Intake form is live in internal Confluence and linked from AE/SE playbooks
Triaging rubric validated on 6 historical requests (retrospective scoring) and adjusted as needed
Prioritized 3-wave language backlog published and socialized with Eng/Design/Support
Security gating checklist integrated with security review flow for any request scoring >=14
Sample SDK snippets for auth refresh and a streaming resume example committed to the SDK repo
stakeholders: Engineering: Liam Chen (assignee), Maria Gonzales (runtime lead)
Customer Success / AE: list TBD per intake
risks_and_tradeoffs: Ship breadth vs depth: supporting many languages increases maintenance and testing burden; prefer 3-wave approach
Auth complexity: adding multiple enterprise auth flows increases surface area for bugs and security issues; require security review on P0/P1
Streaming primitives: exposing low-level primitives gives power to customers but complicates SDK ergonomics; prefer opinionated helpers with escape hatches
Regulatory gating: some enterprise requests will require Private deployment changes, which may add multi-week procurement windows
next_steps: Review draft playbook with Eng (runtime + SDK) and Security on 2025-02-22
Run rubric retrospective on 6 closed SDK requests by 2025-02-28
Publish Confluence playbook and intake form by 2025-03-03
Create sub-issues for first-wave SDK tasks (JS/TS auth refresh sample, Python streaming resume example) after approvals
